properties.description:
Two checks in `tools/skill_lint.py`, run by CI. The first asserts every skill carries a `composes:` declaration — an undeclared skill is invisible to the second, so silence there would read as compliance. The second checks each skill against the obligations of the classes it declares AND NO OTHERS, which is the property no other check in the file can express: everything else there is a predicate over all skills.

⚠️ WHAT IT CANNOT CHECK, and it is the same limit the whole idea carries: whether the obligation was met HONESTLY. It confirms a skill says something that carries the meaning; it cannot confirm the sentence is true or useful. Requiring a section produces a section.

📌 THE OBLIGATIONS ARE TUPLES OF ACCEPTABLE PHRASINGS deliberately, because a single literal fails on wording rather than substance — measured at 13 false failures out of 29 on the first run. The governing line is in the code beside them: adding a phrasing for the same obligation is legitimate, removing the obligation is not.
properties.findings:
PASSING 2026-08-28, after fourteen real omissions were fixed. `python3 tools/skill_lint.py` — all checks passed.

⭐ IT WAS OBSERVED FAILING FIRST, THREE TIMES, AND EACH FAILURE CHANGED SOMETHING:

RUN 1 — 29 unmet. Reading them showed 13 were MATCHING ARTIFACTS rather than deficiencies (`brainstorm` says "searched before", `check-health` says "lose" not "lost"). Obligations became tuples of acceptable phrasings.

RUN 2 — 16 unmet, of which 11 were the SAME obligation. That concentration was the signal: "search before creating" is not owed by every writer, because `genesis` runs on an empty graph, `impact-check` records an event and `parallel-work` records a claim. MINTS was split out of WRITES. **The class was wrong, not the skills.**

RUN 3 — 14 unmet, every one real: 8 skills that mint concept nodes never said to search first; `impact-check` and `link-artifacts` did not bound what they failed to establish; `parallel-work` did not name what a merge can lose; `root-cause` did not name the loop check. Fixed with prose written for each skill.

RUN 4 — 1 unmet, and it was the documented trap: the new `impact-check` text wrapped "could not\\nestablish" across a newline, which `OPTIMIZE_CONTRACT`'s own comment predicts ("fails on reflow rather than on meaning, which trains people to weaken the check"). THE LINE WAS REFLOWED; THE CHECK WAS NOT WEAKENED.

The existing tool-reference check then caught `accept_divergence` named as a tool when it is a parameter of `export_graph` — added to NON_TOOL_TERMS in the same diff, as that check instructs.

Full suite green alongside: `cargo test --workspace` exit 0 from cargo's own code, 165 suites, 1865 passed, 0 failed — byte-identity across all three trees re-verified after 69 frontmatter edits and 33 appended sections.
properties.name: Every skill declares its attribute classes, and meets the obligations of the ones it declares
